author: cinammoncroc000
body:
Hello! This is just a thought I had in my head while I was fooling around with the new 1.8 snapshots.
If you didn't know already, 1.8 is adding a new enchant called Depth Strider. It is a boots-exclusive enchantment that allows you to move faster in water. At its maximum level III (3,) you can swim in water as fast as you can walk on land. Also, speed potions (and maybe slowness?) will affect your in-water speed (only if you have maximum level III Depth Strider.)

Alongside that, the sponge finally has a purpose; it deletes any water blocks (flowing or source) that touch it, along with other adjacent water blocks. (I suggest fooling around with the snapshot to fully understand it; it gets a bit complicated.) And if you fully submerge the sponge in water, it will delete a small sphere of water around it. When sponge soaks up the water, it becomes a wet sponge which ultimately does nothing. However, if you smelt the wet sponge, it will turn back into a regular sponge, ready to soak up more water.
Moreover, the underwater bow mechanics have been changed. When you shoot a bow underwater, the arrow will have full velocity for about half a second, as if it was shot on land. However, after that short frame of time, it completely stops horizontal momentum and sinks down. Better for close-range bow shots and-who knows, underwater bow spam?
Also, you can now brew Water Breathing potions with Pufferfish (which was added in 1.7 but is still a pretty cool feature.)

With all these features in mind, I thought it may be possible to make a fully underwater map. You could start off with a pair of boots enchanted with Depth Strider III, a helmet with Respiration III, and a Speed I effect, which could somewhat simulate on-land movement.

It's just an idea, but I think it's possible and could provide unique gameplay. What are your thoughts?

P.S. OCN is really freaking out about the new TNT mechanics xD

replies.author: cinammoncroc000
replies.body:
I see where you're coming from.
As for people simply swimming straight to the monuments, it probably wouldn't be as easy as it sounds. Good map makers know how to design maps in order for gameplay to be balanced; they would simply adapt the building styles and techniques in order to suit underwater gameplay. And also, being underwater still reduces full movement regardless of Depth Strider + Speed buffs, as well as increasing the amount of time it takes to mine a block (which can be partially fixed by Aqua Affinity - another factor to think about.)

Maps would have to be, like you said, heavily tweaked in order for gameplay to be balanced and fun, but I think it's very possible. :)
